title: Certify finite leaf-destination perturbation envelopes
body:
The quadratic joint-disturbance result in `dirty-interval-coefficient-boundary` explicitly leaves actual leaf-destination errors open. This package completes the finite first step: all 8,120,332 post-leaf/later-cut pairs for n = 1..32 in both orientations have sharp supported-error envelopes 1..5. At n = 16 the maximum is 4, versus 14 for arbitrary joint disturbances.

The new free noncommutative column engine gives rigorous contraction upper bounds; scalar sign assignments attain every maximum. Source emitter binding, separate recursive-prefix oracle checks, 136,260 literal small scalar-sign intervals and five support/domain controls pass. Python 3.12 registered replay and diff check pass.

This is finite evidence, explicitly partial toward the all-size question. It does not infer a logarithmic theorem for all n, internal leaf or cumulative rounding bounds, production precision, or kappa. Exact source pins, task draw, receipt and structured next question included. Credit Arham Tahir and the PR628 precision lineage. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

Base: `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. [Coordinated research batch](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18922638); round 15. The selected record is unchanged.
